terms.short: Where today's IV sits in its 252-session range: (IV − min) ÷ (max − min) × 100. 0 = at the low, 100 = at the high. Not the percentile.
terms.long: Fixture: iv30_cm 12.81 in a 8.50–28.87 range → rank 21. One spike stretches the range and pulls every later rank down. Badge `arithmetic`.

terms.short: The share of the last 252 sessions whose IV was below today's. 60 means IV was lower on 60 % of those days. Not the rank.
terms.long: Same fixture, percentile 60 while the rank is 21. OMON's old "IV rank" was a percentile of the saw-tooth near-expiry series; both now show, each by its definition.

terms.short: ATM IV at a fixed horizon (30 / 60 / 90 days), interpolated in variance between the two expiries that bracket it, the way India VIX is built.
terms.long: Weekly expiries make near-expiry ATM IV saw-tooth with the calendar, so a history needs a fixed horizon: σ²·T is interpolated linearly in T, then annualised.

terms.short: The forward implied by traded options: F = K + (C − P)·e^{rT} at the strike nearest spot where both the call and the put traded.
terms.long: No dividend input needed. Fallback, stored as forward_source: parity → matching future (also if they differ > 0.5 %) → spot·e^{rT}. NIFTY 3 Nov 2026: 23,931.23.

terms.short: 25-delta put IV minus 25-delta call IV, each strike found by inverting its own delta. Positive = puts dearer than calls; NIFTY runs 2–3 vol points.
terms.long: Interpolated to 30 days as skew_25d_30. It is why India VIX sits ≈ 1 vol point above the ATM iv30_cm. A `context` number in the neutral token: it describes, does not predict.

terms.short: Realised vol from the daily high–low range: √(mean ln(H/L)² ÷ 4 ln 2) × √252 over 20 sessions. Needs only high and low.
terms.long: Uses more of each day than close-to-close, so it is less noisy over 20 sessions; it ignores overnight gaps, which is why Yang-Zhang is shown beside it.

terms.short: Realised vol from open, high, low and close: overnight variance + k·open-to-close variance + (1 − k)·Rogers-Satchell, annualised × √252.
terms.long: k = 0.34 ÷ (1.34 + (n + 1)/(n − 1)). The one estimator here that handles overnight gaps; indices take OHLC from index_ohlc_daily, stocks from nse_bhavcopy.

terms.short: NSE Clearing's own volatility per F&O underlying: an EWMA of squared log returns with λ = 0.995, annualised × √365 (not √252).
terms.long: σ²ₜ = 0.995·σ²ₜ₋₁ + 0.005·rₜ². FOVOLT_DDMMYYYY.csv, published ≈ 17:00 IST (16:58 and 17:01 measured); the vol margins are set on. A `context` line beside IV.

terms.short: The clearing corporation's initial margin: the worst loss of the whole position over 16 price × vol scenarios, plus spread charges, with a short-option minimum.
terms.long: Spreads earn offsets: a NIFTY condor needed ₹81,497.07 in Breeze. The 12 %-of-notional estimate measured 4.8× too high. OSTR: Breeze → NSE SPAN file → heuristic.

terms.short: The flat extra margin added on top of SPAN: a percentage of notional per underlying that earns no spread offset.
terms.long: Breeze returns it as non_span_margin_required; total margin = SPAN + exposure. Both are `arithmetic`: an exchange rule, not a view.

terms.short: Each member's share of the index move in points: previous index level × its weight × its return. Additive, so any horizon is the sum of its days.
terms.long: L from NSE's daily index file, r from adjusted closes, w rebuilt from filings and calibrated to NSE's top-10 file. An identity shown with its residual; it describes, does not predict.

terms.short: The index move minus the sum of member points on a day: what the identity does not explain. The fit chip prints it beside the MAE.
terms.long: Comes from stale weights between filings, a missing close and the bank index's capping. A 60-session MAE above 25 points marks the fit `degraded`.

terms.short: The driver leader changes only when a challenger has led the incumbent by ≥ 1.3× (20-session) or 1.2× (60-session) for 5 consecutive sessions.
terms.long: Without it the top name flipped 63 times in 208 sessions; with it, 5 times. The raw leader is stored beside the held one. No colour on the leader; it describes, does not predict.

terms.short: NSE's portfolio-wise futures-equivalent open interest: options OI weighted by delta and added to futures, per stock, across exchanges.
terms.long: From combineoi_deleq_DDMMYYYY.csv (≈ 19:18 IST). Shown with the % of MWPL as a `context` column on OMON and DERV, never coloured.

terms.short: The market-wide position limit for a stock's F&O book. OI above 95 % of it puts the stock in the F&O ban (no new positions) until it falls below 80 %.
terms.long: The MWPL zip lands ≈ 19:23 IST; the ban list (≈ 19:24) is named for the next session; clients holding ≥ 3 % of the limit come as a file dated the previous session.

terms.short: The volatility that makes an option's model price equal its market price: a price restated in vol units, quoted annualised in vol points.
terms.long: Computed per traded strike with Black-76 on the parity forward; an untraded strike carries NSE's theoretical settle, so it gets no IV (price_source flags it).

terms.short: Black's option model on the forward rather than the spot: the convention behind every stored IV and Greek, named by model_version (b76-pcp-v1).
terms.long: T = calendar days ÷ 365 at the 15:30 close; r recorded on every row; a change of convention is a new model_version and new rows, never an overwrite.

terms.short: IV interpolated at the forward, not at the nearest strike. Near = the first expiry with more than 2 days left; monthly = the first expiry 20–60 days out.
terms.long: Expiry-day and T ≤ 2 d rows stay in the surface but are left out of "near": their IV jumps with the calendar.

terms.short: One expiry's ATM IV from listing to expiry: the series that follows a single contract through its life.
IV plotted against strike for one expiry; stored in log-moneyness ln(K ÷ F) so surfaces compare across days.
IV by expiry. The slope iv90_cm − iv30_cm is positive when far months are dearer, the usual state, and often inverts around events.
terms.long: A `context` number: it describes, does not predict.

terms.short: The volatility the price delivered: close-to-close σ of 20 daily log returns × √252, shown beside the Parkinson, Yang-Zhang and FOVOLT estimates.
IV minus realised vol: what options price over what the index has been delivering. A `context` spread in the neutral token, never coloured.
terms.long: The "IV paid vs vol delivered" ledger over the last 12 monthly expiries shows how often the premium exceeded the move; it describes, does not predict.

terms.short: The one-standard-deviation move the options price in: ATM IV × √T to expiry, or iv30_cm ÷ √252 for one day. A model's arithmetic, not a forecast.
terms.long: The hit-rate panel counts how often the realised move stayed inside it over 60 sessions.

terms.short: ATM call + ATM put at one expiry: the market's price for movement in either direction. Its decay through the day is the expiry-day curve.
The change in near-expiry ATM IV across a results release: IV after ÷ IV before − 1, kept per stock with the implied and the realised move.
terms.long: The EVTS ledger lists the last 8 releases per stock (IV before and after, implied vs realised move); it describes, does not predict.

terms.short: NSE's model-free 30-day volatility index from NIFTY option prices (a variance strip over the OTM wings). Stored as OHLC in vix_daily, one source for every page.
terms.long: Nightly from the ind_close_all file; a one-off backfill from NSE's historicalOR/vixhistory (≤ 1 year per call). It includes the skew, so it sits above ATM iv30_cm.

terms.short: The rate in the model: a dated constant (6.5 %, O-T5) recorded as r on every stored row, so a later change never rewrites history.
terms.long: With the forward taken from parity the rate barely matters: 100 bp moves a 30-day ATM NIFTY IV by ≈ 0.01 vol point.

terms.short: Put open interest ÷ call open interest on an expiry. A `context` ratio shown uncoloured: it says which side holds more open contracts, nothing more.
Contracts outstanding at the close, per strike and expiry; its daily change is a `context` column. OI-change classes tested as a swing rule showed no edge (H2).
NSE Clearing's own delta per option contract (Contract_Delta file, ≈ 18:30–19:20 IST), shown beside our Black-76 delta; a gap above 0.05 is logged.
NSE Clearing's end-of-day SPAN parameters (risk arrays per contract, spread charges, short-option minimum), ≈ 17:02 IST. Lets OSTR price margin offline.
terms.long: No scheduled job downloads it yet: the parser and the fallback read whatever file sits in data/nse_archive/span/.

terms.short: The member with the largest |points| over a rolling 20- or 60-session window, held with hysteresis; shown in the neutral token with its tenure and share.
terms.long: "20-session leader BHARTIARTL for N sessions, 12.5 % of member points" says what moved the index; it describes, does not predict.

terms.short: The members' equal-weight return minus the cap-weight (index) return over 20 sessions, in percentage points. Negative = a few heavyweights carried the index.
terms.long: A `context` number; "narrow" or "broad" describes, does not predict.

terms.short: How few names explain the move: the top-5 share of |points|, the Herfindahl of contributions and of weights, and 1 ÷ Σ weight² (effective number of names).
Rebuilt weights are scaled to NSE's daily top-10 file (≈ 16:30 IST): iwf_correction = official ÷ rebuilt for the ten names, the other forty pro rata, Σ = 100.
terms.long: NSE publishes no full daily weight file for free and the equity-stockIndices endpoint is dead (404). The calibrated rebuild explained 99.6 % of daily variance.

terms.short: Every stored row carries the period it describes, when the publisher released it and when we first saw it; a source revision is a new row, never an overwrite.
terms.long: Derived tables keep the latest computation per key; a past vintage is recomputed from the archived source files, which ingest_log versions by sha256.

terms.short: A re-fetch whose body changed (sha256) is logged as revision + 1 with the publisher's Last-Modified; the 22:45 pass re-checks the equity bhavcopy this way.
terms.long: NSE re-published the 4 Nov equity bhavcopy at 22:05 IST, after a first evening copy. Note: NSE's Last-Modified header is GMT; add 5:30 for IST.

terms.short: The IST time by which the terminal expects a dataset stored, trading-day aware. Past it the DATA view shows amber, past its lag budget red. No composite score.
terms.long: Page wording: "stored 30 Oct · expected by 21:00 · 3 sessions behind · catch-up 19:30 tomorrow". States: live, fresh, amber, red, gap.

terms.short: An explicit row saying a session-bound capture (pre-open book, breadth samples, FII/DII, gold open) was lost while the stack was down; pages say so.
The chip on every panel header: LIVE Breeze, LIVE NSE, DELAYED with its age, STALE, OFFLINE or GAP. Daily data shows its date, not a clock.
Each derived number's label: `arithmetic` (identity or model convention), `context` (a description), `heuristic` (a house rule, its error shown). No `signal` exists.
terms.long: `signal` needs a FINDINGS PASS row from a pre-registered study (PIT data, |t| ≥ 2 in the full sample and both halves, after costs). None has passed here.

terms.short: Calendar days from the trade date to the expiry at the 15:30 close; T = dte ÷ 365 in the model. Read from the file, never assumed from a weekday.
One ledger every ICICI Breeze call passes through: per-minute and per-day counters in SQLite, per-caller quotas, a hard stop at the owner's cap.
terms.long: The documented 100/min and 5,000/day are the ceiling; the owner's cap (O-T6) is the budget. The 15-minute chain pilot and the margin calls share it.
